title: How to Become More Likeable at Work
summary: The creator explains that being more likeable leads to more help and career opportunities, claiming it helped him get three promotions in 15 months. He shares three daily habits to build likeability: opening up by focusing on others, becoming a better listener by avoiding 'me too' responses, and becoming an encouraging leader.
key_points: The creator claims that when choosing between two equally competent people, employers will always promote the more likeable person.
First habit: Get comfortable opening up to people by overcoming the fear of rejection and judgment.
Shift your focus from 'me, myself, and I' to making the other person feel special, laugh, and feel good about themselves.
Alternatively, learn something at the start of the day and spend the entire day applying it so you are too focused to worry about judgment.
Second habit: Become a better listener instead of just waiting for your turn to speak.
Resist the urge to say 'me too' or 'I have a similar experience' when someone else is talking.
Instead, ask them more questions about what they said so they feel heard, seen, and like you more.
Third habit: Become encouraging, which is especially important for leadership positions.
When complimenting someone, always give context using the formula: 'Thank you for doing this thing. I like that you did this thing. That was a great idea, most people didn't think of that.'
content:
Instagram reel/post by Maarij | Simplifying People Skills.
Text / caption: How to become more likeable
Here's how to become more likable at work, because the more likable you are, the more people will want to help you. The more people want to help you, the more opportunities that you're going to get, which is why I was able to get three promotions back to back within 15 months when I was an employee. And now that I'm an employer, if I have the choice between two people, both equally competent, I will always promote the one who is more likable. And there's only three things that you need to remember to be more likable every single day. The first is, you need to get comfortable opening up to people first. And the reason why most people struggle with this is because they have a little bit of fear of rejection or the fear of judgment, what will other people think of me. But if you wait for the world to open up to you, you're going to be waiting for the rest of your life. So you might as well lead your life and open up first. And there's two things that will help you get rid of that fear of rejection or that fear of judgment. First, you need to stop thinking about yourself, me, myself, and I, and you need to focus on how do I make the other person feel special? How do I make them laugh? How do I make them feel good about themselves? Shifting the focus from you to them. But the second method is a little bit easier to implement, which is if you learn something at the start of the day, then focus your entire day on implementing what you learned, you will be too focused on applying what you learned that you won't be thinking about yourself, which is why you won't be worried about your fear of judgment or fear of rejection. Which leads me to the second point. You need to become a better listener. Most people when they're in a conversation, are only listening so that they get an opportunity to speak themselves, which is why what I want you to do instead is focus on resisting the urge to say me too. So whenever someone else is talking, we have this urge inside of us, this instinct that we should relate to them, we should say, oh, I have a similar experience. If you can just resist the instinct to say I have had a similar experience, me too, I understand what you're going through, and just focus on asking them more questions about what they said, they will feel heard, they will feel seen, they will like you more, which leads me to the last and probably the most important, which is if you want to go into more leadership positions, it is way more important to have this trait than to actually be really good at what you do, because as a leader, you're more responsible for taking care of the team and making sure that they get the job done. So if you can adopt this one habit, you're most likely going to get promoted as well, which is you need to become encouraging. So what I want you to do is when you're complimenting, give some context. Thank you for doing this thing. I like that you did this thing. That was a great idea. Most people didn't think of that. Compliment plus context.
